options.text: A slow query is locking the database
options.why: The database is at 41% and its slow-query log is empty: it is waiting on the app servers, not the other way round.

options.text: Twice the usual traffic, and the app servers are full
options.why: Requests doubled at 19:00, exactly when the ad aired, and every app server is at 100% CPU. Add app servers until the peak fits.

options.text: This afternoon's deploy has a bug
options.why: The deploy went out at 14:10 and error rates were flat for five hours. Rolling back would cost time and change nothing.

diagnosis.question: Orders fail and menus still load. Why?

options.text: The cache is serving stale data
options.why: Menus come from the cache and still work; orders do not touch the cache at all.

options.text: A network partition between the zones
options.why: Every app server reaches the cache and the queue fine; only the database host is gone.

options.text: The database primary died, and there is no replica to promote
options.why: One database box is a single point of failure: when it goes, every write goes with it. Run a replica so a failover takes seconds, not a restore.

ticket.title: PAGE: menus slow, traffic up 3x, conversion flat

diagnosis.question: Traffic tripled but orders did not. What is it?

options.text: A marketing launch nobody told us about
options.why: Real users order: a launch would raise orders with menus. Orders are flat.

options.text: Bots scraping menus with random ids
options.why: Requests come from a few thousand IPs, hit random restaurant ids (so the cache misses) and never order. Stop them at the edge with a firewall before they reach the app servers.

options.text: Mobile apps retrying in a loop
options.why: The retries would be for orders and come from our own app's user agent; these requests do not.

ticket.title: PAGE: database CPU 100% after the cache upgrade

diagnosis.question: The cache was upgraded at 18:55 and the database caught fire at 18:56. Why?

options.text: The new cache version is slower
options.why: Cache latency is 1 ms as before. It is not slow; it is empty.

options.text: A missing index on the menus table
options.why: The same queries ran fine yesterday at the same traffic. Nothing changed in the database.

options.text: The cache restarted empty, and every miss goes to the database at once
options.why: A cold cache sends almost every read to the database until it warms up. Keep enough read capacity behind the cache (replicas) to survive a cold start, and warm caches before a restart.

diagnosis.question: One of three zones is gone. What do you check first?

options.text: Fail everything over to another region
options.why: A region failover takes hours and loses recent writes. Two zones are still up: the question is what ran only in the dead one.

options.text: What ran as a single instance: it was in that zone, and it is gone
options.why: A zone takes a third of every component's replicas, and all of anything you ran once. Two or three of everything, spread over zones, turns a zone outage into lost capacity instead of an outage.

options.text: DNS: clients still resolve to the dead zone
options.why: The load balancer's health checks already stopped sending traffic there; DNS points at the load balancer.
